title: Daily routine
sub: Je me lève à sept heures
can: Describe your day with reflexive verbs, say when you do things, and say how often.
doneText: You can now describe your day, from getting up to going to bed, and say how often you do things.

discover.intro: Blue sentences have a small extra word before the verb. Orange sentences do not. Spot what it is.

groups.label: Blue
lines: Je me lève à sept heures.
Tu te lèves à huit heures.
Elle se lève à neuf heures.

discover.question: What is the extra word in the blue sentences?
options: Me, te or se. The action is done to yourself, and the little word changes with the person: je me, tu te, elle se.
A word for the time, like à.
discover.nudge: Not quite. Look straight before each verb in blue: lève, lèves, lève. What comes just before?
discover.reveal: These are reflexive verbs: the action goes back to the person who does it. Je me lève is literally I raise myself. The little word matches the person:

hooks.title: The order of the day
rows: Ensuite, je prends le petit déjeuner.

learn.title: Reflexive verbs and your day
learn.sub: Tap any form to hear it

blocks.title: Le matin or du matin
a: Je me lève à sept heures du matin.
I get up at seven in the morning.
b: Le matin, je me lève tôt.
In the morning, I get up early.
blocks.note: Du matin comes after a clock time: sept heures du matin. Le matin on its own means in the morning in general. It works the same with le soir and l'après-midi.

blocks.text: The little word goes straight before the verb: je me lève, never je lève me. With a vowel, me and te shorten: je m'habille, tu t'habilles.
In a negative, ne … pas wraps the little word and the verb together: je ne me lève pas tôt. Ne goes before me. Jamais works like pas: je ne me couche jamais tôt.
Breakfast in France is small: a coffee, and bread with butter and jam, or a croissant. Lunch is often the main meal, and dinner is usually around eight.

phrases.es: Je me lève à sept heures.

phrases.en: I have a shower in the morning.

phrases.es: Je vais au travail en métro.
phrases.en: I go to work by métro.

phrases.es: Je ne me lève pas tôt.

exercises.say: Je me couche à onze heures.
options: I go to bed at eleven
exercises.why: Je me couche is I go to bed.

exercises.prompt: Rapid fire: me, te or se?

items.full: Tu te lèves à huit heures.

items.why: On goes with se, like il.

items.full: Il se douche à sept heures.

exercises.why: Tu goes with lèves, with an s.
Je ne me lève pas: the verb stays in the middle.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.
exercises.sentence: Tu me lèves à huit heures.
exercises.fixed: Tu te lèves à huit heures.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.
exercises.why: Il goes with couche, with no s.

answer: je me lève à sept heures
exercises.why: Je me lève: the little word me goes before the verb.

answer: je ne me lève pas tôt
exercises.why: Ne goes before me, and pas goes after the verb.

exercises.prompt: First, I get up. Then I have breakfast.
exercises.answer: D'abord, je me lève. Ensuite, je prends le petit déjeuner.
exercises.why: D'abord and ensuite put your day in order.

exercises.prompt: Which is right for I go to bed?
exercises.why: The little word goes before the verb, and je goes with me.

exercises.prompt: Which means in the morning, in general?
exercises.why: Le matin is in the morning in general. Du matin follows a clock time.

write.title: Say it in your own words
write.task: Describe your morning, using d'abord and ensuite.
write.starter: D'abord, je me lève à…  Ensuite…
write.model: D'abord, je me lève à sept heures. Ensuite, je prends le petit déjeuner. Après, je vais au travail.
checklist: Me, te or se goes before the verb
D'abord, ensuite and après put it in order

boss.title: Chatting with your flatmate Baptiste
boss.persona: You are Baptiste, a friendly student who shares a flat in Lyon with the learner. Talk about your morning and evening routines and what time you get up and go to bed. Address the learner as tu. Keep every message to one short sentence.

turns.npc: Salut. Tu te lèves à quelle heure, toi ?
turns.en: Hi. What time do you get up?
choices: Je me lève à sept heures.
Je lève à sept heures.
The little word is missing: je me lève.
Je me lèves à sept heures.
Je goes with lève, with no s.

turns.npc: Tôt ! Moi, je me lève à dix heures le week-end.
turns.en: Early. Me, I get up at ten at the weekend.
choices: Moi, je ne me lève pas tard.
Moi, je ne lève pas me tard.
Me goes straight before the verb: je ne me lève pas.
Moi, je me ne lève pas tard.
Ne comes before me: je ne me lève pas.

turns.npc: Et le soir, tu te couches à quelle heure ?
turns.en: And in the evening, what time do you go to bed?
choices: Je me couche à onze heures.
Je me couches à onze heures.
Je goes with couche, with no s.
Tu te couches à onze heures.
You are talking about yourself, so je me couche, not tu te couches.

turns.npc: Bon, je vais me coucher. Bonne nuit.
turns.en: Right, I'm going to bed. Good night.
choices: Bonne nuit, Baptiste. À demain.
Bon matin, Baptiste. À demain.
Bon matin is not what people say in France. At night, say bonne nuit.
Bonne nuit, Baptiste. À hier.
Hier is yesterday. See you tomorrow is à demain.

boss.chatOpeningEn: Do you often go to bed late?
